_note: V1.8's occasions, on the effects channel src/core/law.gd shares with them -- the SEVENTH directory on data/diplomatic-actions/'s shape and the last content type the V1 tier adds. A GLOBAL FLAT LIST, on data/pledges/' argument: an event names no place, no firm and no institution, and its subject is an OFFICE all ten nations fill, so none of these is true of France in a way it is not true of Germany. U6c's correction does not apply -- what made per-project geography per-NATION was a coordinate, and there is no coordinate on this channel. At V4.4 the category grows to sixteen, and the register's argument does not move: a revelation arrives whether or not it is deserved.
_scandal_note: THE ONLY V1-TIERED MECHANIC SECTION 8 OWNS IS THIS ONE. Counting docs/brainstorm/mechanics-*.md's tier column found section 8's own two bullets tiered nowhere at all, and every event-shaped mechanic in those four tables tiered Someday -- Terrorism, Pandemics and global crises, Emergency powers, the housing market. Scandals came here from section 5 at V1.5d, on that box's own argument, and they arrive with a framing channel already built: docs/media-model.md's per-bloc salience gain is what decides who hears about it.
_subject_note: Each of these names an OFFICE and never a person. U6b's rule verbatim -- a law names an office, the nation's own government block names who holds it -- so nothing in src/sim/ ever touches a person id and src/ui/main.gd resolves the label at card time. It is also why the same scandal reads correctly in a republic and in a monarchy.
_default_note: Exactly one choice on each event carries `default: true`, and it is what happens when the player says nothing. That is required rather than inferred from the ordering, because it is the whole of *forces a response under time pressure*: the deadline is only pressure if the silence costs something. Every default here is strictly worse than at least one alternative on at least one axis, measured on a live path by tools/events_probe.gd table E3 rather than asserted from these numbers -- docs/pledge-model.md's own dominance test was the wrong test because the deciding quantity was nowhere in the content.

events.name: The procurement files
events.summary: A newspaper has the ministry's contract file. The awards went to two firms, and one of them wrote the specification.
events.speaker_line: We are prepared to print, and the only thing that would change my mind is a good reason you have not given us yet.

choices.label: Dismiss the minister
choices.summary: Decisive, and it disowns your own side. The city reads it as cleaning house; the countryside and business read it as feeding a minister to the press.

choices.label: Order an inquiry
choices.summary: Slower, milder and it costs nobody anything today. It also cleans up a good deal less.

choices.label: Refuse to comment
choices.summary: The file does not go away and neither does the story.

events.name: The honours list
events.summary: Two names on the head of state's honours list gave money to the governing party. Nobody says the two facts are connected, and nobody says they are not.
events.speaker_line: My readers deserve to know what the honours were for, and I am giving you the first chance to say.

choices.label: Distance the government
choices.summary: Let the press have it. It is not your list and you say so.

choices.label: Defend the office
choices.summary: The office is above this. Saying so buys you the people who agree and costs you the people who do not.

choices.label: Let it pass
choices.summary: It does not pass.

events.name: The broadcasting charter
events.summary: The state broadcaster's charter is up. Its newsroom has spent the year on your government, and the terms of the renewal are yours to set.
events.speaker_line: If the renewal is written to punish a newsroom, I will make that argument loudly and in public.

choices.label: Tighten the terms
choices.summary: A quieter newsroom, and everybody notices that it went quiet.

choices.label: Guarantee its independence
choices.summary: You will be covered as badly as before and you will be seen to have allowed it.

choices.label: Renew it unchanged
choices.summary: Nobody thanks a government for a decision it did not make.

events.name: The uncertified accounts
events.summary: The auditors have refused to certify the governing party's annual accounts. Donations were booked as loans, the loans as gifts, and the law that says a party without certified accounts cannot stand at the next election is older than anyone's desire to test it.
events.speaker_line: The auditors will not certify the party's accounts, and the law about who may stand at elections has waited years for a test.

choices.label: Regularise the record
choices.summary: An amnesty law, passed in a hurry, legalising what the audit found. The accounts close; the question of what they closed over does not.

choices.label: Put the parties on the public purse
choices.summary: A fixed sum per vote, and no more private money anywhere. It buys clean hands at the taxpayer's price, and in the constituencies it reads as politicians paying themselves.

choices.label: Let the law run
choices.summary: You did not write the law and you will not suspend it. The party's lawyers spend the summer on it, and every editorial page spends it on you.

events.name: The memo
events.summary: A cabinet minute is on a newspaper's front page. It is the health ministry's own paper, and it prices the winter waiting lists in stories a month: 'manageable until the autumn, political after'.
events.speaker_line: I am not the one who leaked it, but I will not pretend the public does not have a right to read it.

choices.label: Find the leaker
choices.summary: The services are asked to examine their own government's paperwork and the pressroom's phone records. Other governments will learn what can be asked; the pressroom learns it faster.

choices.label: Publish the whole file
choices.summary: The memo is damning only in company. Released with the twelve pages around it, it reads as a government doing arithmetic, and the paper loses the story it was keeping warm.

choices.label: Wait for the news cycle
choices.summary: It does not finish on its own; it waits for your next mistake.

events.name: The internal review
events.summary: A serving official has sent a newspaper the ministry's internal review of a defence programme: forty per cent over, three years late, and written eleven months before the minister told the assembly otherwise.
events.speaker_line: A serving official has sent us the defence review, forty per cent over and three years late, which makes my day and will ruin somebody's year.

choices.label: Prosecute the official
choices.summary: The state's case is airtight and the sentence will be a warning to every other official holding a file. The press's case is that this is what the law is for.

choices.label: Protect the disclosure
choices.summary: Publish the review in full and dare the ministry to say which line was untrue. The programme still costs what it costs; only now the assembly prices it with the file open.

choices.label: Release the summary
choices.summary: The conclusions without the tables: enough to say the review exists, never enough to check it against what was said. The official keeps their career and the press keeps the story.

events.name: The minister's shares
events.summary: The renewal contracts for the regions' water testing went to a consortium in which the housing minister's spouse has held a share since March. The minister signed the delegation in February and says the two dates are the point.
events.speaker_line: The water testing contracts went to a consortium the housing minister's spouse holds shares in, and the minister insists the two dates settle it, which my lawyers find charming.

choices.label: Force the divestment
choices.summary: The share goes into a blind trust this week and the minister offers the assembly a full accounting. It is the clean version, and it costs a competent minister a quarter of their attention.

choices.label: Say the rules were followed
choices.summary: They were -- the declaration is dated, filed, and read by nobody. You defend the letter of the register, and the register takes the reputation damage with you.

choices.label: Move the portfolio
choices.summary: The minister keeps their seat and loses water testing; the contracts keep their signatory. Everyone reads it as exactly what it is.

events.name: The register of meetings
events.summary: The backbench bill to publish who lobbies whom, and on whose lunch, has died twice in committee. Its third reading is scheduled because its sponsor has the votes and nothing left to lose.
events.speaker_line: I will print who votes for transparency and who prefers the lunches, so choose your side before my readers do it for you.

choices.label: Adopt the register
choices.summary: Every meeting with a minister, published within a month. The government loses the quiet corridor and keeps the corridor; the lobbying firms lose a business model.

choices.label: Take the publication out
choices.summary: A register that records meetings nobody may read: the bill passes, the corridor stays quiet, and the sponsor's press release writes itself.

choices.label: Let it die in committee
choices.summary: It has died there twice and the committee knows how. The corridor keeps its silence and the sponsor keeps his grievance.

events.name: The appointment
events.summary: The new director of the regional health agencies is the labour minister's brother-in-law. The selection panel that interviewed him did not interview anyone else, which the panel's own minutes record without embarrassment.
events.speaker_line: Readers will want to know why only one name was ever considered, and I mean to put that question to the government.

choices.label: Rescind the appointment
choices.summary: The post is re-advertised and the panel reformed, and the health agencies run for six months without a director. The minister keeps his job and loses the argument that his family is separate from his office.

choices.label: Call him the best candidate
choices.summary: The defence is true in the way such defences are true: the field was narrow because the field was drawn. You spend the government's credibility on a brother-in-law, and the base notices you paid it for family.

choices.label: Send it to the auditors
choices.summary: The appointment stands while the auditors read the minutes. They will take a season, and the story takes a season with it.

events.name: The expense claims
events.summary: The expenses review has reached the housing allowance, and the pattern is not ambiguity: flats designated as second homes at the address of party offices, and one member's garden shed claimed as a constituency office. Four hundred members are in the sample; the worst twenty will be on the front page for a month.
events.speaker_line: We have read the housing allowances closely, and I can promise you the garden shed will keep my readers warm all month.

choices.label: Publish the claims in full
choices.summary: Every member's ledger, online, this week. The government's own side supplies the worst pages, and the clearing of the air is felt in the constituencies as a clearing of the decks.

choices.label: Order repayment and cap the allowance
choices.summary: The twenty repay, the allowance drops to a schedule written by the treasury, and the members' anger at the treasury becomes the story's second act. The taxpayer is repaid in full and photographed doing it.

choices.label: Refer the worst twenty
choices.summary: The complaints go to the standards body, which publishes in eighteen months and finds what a newspaper already has. The money mostly stays where it is.

choices.label: Sit on the review
choices.summary: It is not published; it leaks. The same twenty, the same month, and the government now owns the cover as well as the claims.

events.name: The transcripts
events.summary: A newspaper has printed transcripts of calls between one of its reporters and a ministerial adviser, with the interception dates alongside. The government says it never authorised them; the services say the government never asked. Both statements are being read very carefully by the people who wrote them.
events.speaker_line: Interception dates printed beside each call, and both sides swearing the other one asked, that is my gift to you this morning.

choices.label: Appoint an independent judge
choices.summary: A serving judge, a mandate that includes the services' own lawyers, and a report the government does not get to see first. It is the only answer that treats the transcripts as what they are, and the services will treat it as a declaration of war.

choices.label: Let the services investigate themselves
choices.summary: The report will be honest as far as its authors can make it, which is further than its readers will believe. The transcripts stay unexplained and the pressroom stays warned.

choices.label: Pursue the newspaper
choices.summary: The official charge is receiving state documents; the effect is a defence fund with public sympathy and a pressroom that has learned what this government does with a story it cannot have.

events.name: The fee schedule
events.summary: Recordings of a former minister coaching a consultancy's clients before their meetings with his old department have reached the press, together with his fee schedule. The diary the department itself keeps confirms the meetings happened.
events.speaker_line: The recordings and the fee schedule are in my hands, and the diary confirms every meeting, so I would like your line before we print.

choices.label: Legislate the revolving door shut
choices.summary: Two years between office and lobby, on the statute book by autumn. The lobbying firms call it vindictive; the calls it would have caught are the recordings.

choices.label: Hand the file to the prosecutors
choices.summary: What he did may not be a crime; the prosecutors will spend a year establishing which. The fees stop, the story does not.

choices.label: Say the law has no case
choices.summary: True, and now the law is the story: a rules book written by insiders for insiders. You have defended a former colleague with the government's own credibility.

events.name: The undeclared loans
events.summary: The audit office has found the loans: a large sum to the governing coalition's campaign, from a lender with no repayment schedule, no written terms, and -- the auditors note, in the flat prose of their profession -- no apparent memory of being asked.
events.speaker_line: The auditors found loans with no terms, no schedule, and a lender with no memory of being asked, and they wrote that without smiling.

choices.label: Refer it to the courts
choices.summary: The auditors' file goes to the prosecutors unopened by the government. If the money was what it says it was, the party is embarrassed; if it was not, someone else is in the dock.

choices.label: Repay the loans from the public purse
choices.summary: The state settles its own coalition's debts and calls it closing the file. The sum is small; the precedent is not, and the opposition will price the next election on it.

choices.label: Dispute the auditors' reading
choices.summary: The loans were loans, the terms were terms, and the audit office has a political majority. It is a defence that lasts until the lender's next statement, and everyone in the building knows the lender gives statements.

events.name: The captured rulebook
events.summary: The services regulator's draft rulebook matches the industry association's own submission, in places to the comma, and the association's former director-general sits on the drafting panel. The association's next chairman is the regulator's current one; he takes up the post in June.
events.speaker_line: My readers will draw their own conclusion from that rulebook, so help me by giving them a better one.

choices.label: Void the drafts and reform the panel
choices.summary: The rulebook is written again, by people who have never worked for the industry it binds. The deadline it misses is real, and the association's members will spend the gap explaining 'regulatory uncertainty' to the markets.

choices.label: Amend the drafts in the margins
choices.summary: A few clauses tightened, the architecture untouched. The rulebook ships on time with its paternity still legible in every definition.

choices.label: Adopt the rulebook as written
choices.summary: It regulates the industry the way the industry asked to be regulated. The chairman's June move now looks less like a coincidence and more like a title for the whole story.

events.name: The foundation
events.summary: The national literacy foundation has spent five years and forty million in ministry grants, and its consulting fees have gone, every year, to a firm owned by its two founders -- the culture minister's oldest friends, and the source of every reference in the minister's own appointment file.
events.speaker_line: Forty million in grants, five years of consulting fees to the founders' own firm, and the minister's oldest friends in the appointment file, a tidy circle indeed.

choices.label: End the grant
choices.summary: The foundation is wound up and the programmes are folded into the ministry, where nobody consults anybody. The literacy schemes survive; the founders' firm does not.

choices.label: Put the contracts to tender
choices.summary: The foundation stays, the fees are re-tendered under published rules, and the founders' firm is welcome to bid like anyone else. It will not win, which is the point, and the audit that follows is the cost.

choices.label: Let the auditors read the five years
choices.summary: The grant continues at this year's rate while they read. The findings will confirm what the fee schedule already says, at the pace auditors read.

events.name: The development bank's board
events.summary: The state development bank's newest non-executive director is twenty-six. Her consultancy is a year old and lists one client, and her father is the governing party's treasurer, who says the two facts are unrelated and that his daughter is 'a generational talent'.
events.speaker_line: A twenty-six year old director, a one client consultancy, and a treasurer father who calls it coincidence, my printers are already warmed.

choices.label: Block the appointment
choices.summary: The bank's board is told the seat stays open and the procedure is rewritten. The treasurer learns the size of your majority on the board, and the bank's next bond issue answers a question nobody asked about politics in its credit file.

choices.label: Confirm her and defend the choice
choices.summary: The defence is made once, in a statement about widening boards beyond the usual grey faces, and it is true, which does not survive the treasurer's smile on the evening news.

choices.label: Let the appointment stand
choices.summary: No statement, no defence, and the seat filled by the time anyone asks. It works twice; the third time the question is why it always works.
